fields.original: Conspiciendo nosmet ipsos tam miseram, et non stabilem Capellam habere, ideo supplices ad Dominum Nostrum Terrestrem Antonium K. object.kind: A page of a Hungarian state civil register of births, in the form used from 1895 to 1906: one entry to a page
object.why: A printed Hungarian form on green security paper with a page number (320) and an entry number (45 szám). It opens 'Kelt ... Megjelent az alulírott anyakönyvvezető előtt' (dated at ...; appeared before the undersigned registrar) and closes 'Felolvastatván ... helybenhagyatott és aláíratott' (read out, approved and signed), with the registrar's and the informant's signatures. That is the entry itself, taken down in the informant's presence, not a certificate copied from it later: a certificate would carry a seal, a date of issue and no informant's signature. The published description of the collection says that from 1895 to 1906 the forms are one page to an event and from 1907 a row in a table.
object.does_not_fit: The image shows no cover, title page or stamp, so the registry and the archive are not on it. Each register was kept in two copies, the office's own and one sent to the county. Which copy this is cannot be told from the form: whether the informant signed both is not known to this agent. The owner says the image is 'ostensibly from Uzhhorod' (DM-PR-6), which would make it the county's copy, since Ungvár was the seat of Ung county.

Some 250 name boxes over eight or nine generations, with photographs, a coat of arms and two churches. At this size only the photograph captions and a few boxes can be read. Read here: a woman Mary D[e]mko, 1906 to 199[?], born in the United States, apparently at Passaic, New Jersey, with a marriage line naming Vysoká nad Uhom; her parents Andrej D[..]ko and Mária M[...]ová (1887 to 1979), both of Vysoká nad Uhom; his parents Ján D[..]ko and Anna S[...], of the same village; above them a Ján D[..]ko and a Mária. translation: Iňačovce, district of Michalovce, house 117, owner Michal Demko, on the night of 1 December 1930. Michal Demko, head of the household, born 28 August 1882 at Vysoká, married, Greek Catholic, Slovak, a farmer, reads and writes. Zuzanna Demková, his wife, born 28 April 1901 at Iňačovce, married 3 February 1919, two children born. Juraj Demko, son, born 17 September 1911 at Iňačovce, single. Anna Demková, daughter, born 12 November 1924. Maria Kočišová, the head's mother-in-law, born 15 August 1863 at Iňačovce, a widow, married 10 November 1879, three children born and two living, Roman Catholic, reads and writes.
notes: This is Maria Demko's father, twenty-four years after her birth. The registration of 1906 has Mihály Demkó, Greek Catholic, living at Solymos, born at Magasrév, aged 24. This sheet has Michal Demko, Greek Catholic, owner of a house at Iňačovce, born at Vysoká on 28 August 1882. Magasrév and Vysoká are one village.

It shows that a Mihály Demkó born at Vysoká in August 1882 grew up and was alive in 1930. The baptism in hand is of a boy born 19 August 1882 and baptised the 20th (DM-D-001); the census says the 28th. Nine days apart, in the same month of the same year, in a village with one Demko birth that summer in the strips. This is the survival that ledger X-017 asked for (DM-NC-001).

His wife in 1930 is not Maria's mother. Zuzanna was born in 1901 and married him on 3 February 1919. So Mária Kocsis, alive in August 1906, was dead by then. The son Juraj was born in September 1911, when Zuzanna was ten: he is a child of the first marriage, and so a brother of Maria Demko.

The mother-in-law is the find. Maria Kočišová: a widow whose married name is Kocsis, Roman Catholic in a Greek Catholic house, born at Iňačovce in 1863, married in 1879. The one Roman Catholic woman married to a Kocsis at Solymos in the strips is Mária Knyezső, wife of Mihály Kocsis of no. 19, mother of the Mária baptised in [1887] (DM-D-054). The sheet does not say whose mother she is. She may be the mother of his dead first wife, or of Zuzanna, or of both if he married two sisters. See DM-H-041.
Her birthday is 15 August, like the one given for Maria in her in-laws' house at Senné (DM-D-101).
The Duska agent's note gave these dates before this agent read the image. Read from the image; agrees with DUS:D-011-84 in every field read by both.

Ján Demko, head of the household, born 15 April 1875 at Vysoká, married, Slovak, Greek Catholic, reads and writes, a farmer on his own account. Maria, his wife, born in 1878 at Vysoká, Roman Catholic, married in 1897, ten children born and six living. Juraj, their son, born 1908, married, and his wife Maria, born 1911, married in 1929. notes: A Ján Demko, Greek Catholic, born at Vysoká in April 1875 and still farming there in 1930. One János Demkó was baptised at Viszoka in 1875 in the strips in hand: on 29 March, at house 121, son of György Demkó, Greek Catholic farmer, and Mária Hreskó, Roman Catholic (DM-D-014). Same village, rite and year; the day is seventeen days off. He is taken to be that child, the brother of Maria Demko's father (DM-H-045).

This is the sheet that was to test DM-H-037, and it sinks it. The János Demko of Senné no. 87 in 1900 was Roman Catholic, a carpenter, with a Greek Catholic wife from Lasztomér, Mária Ivanko (DM-D-086). This Ján is Greek Catholic, a farmer at Vysoká, with a Roman Catholic wife born at Vysoká whom he married in 1897. Two men.
He is the third son his father named János; the first two died in 1872 and 1873 (DM-NC-020). This one lived to be 55 at least and had ten children.
Like his father he married a Roman Catholic. The sons are entered Greek Catholic, after the father.
